slot.brief: Two thin prisms of different materials and angles combined for no net deviation; set up deviation and dispersion conditions simultaneously to solve for the required prism angles and/or refractive indices.

stem: Two thin prisms are oppositely oriented. Their yellow-light refractive indices are $\mu_A=1.5$ and $\mu_B=1.6$, and their dispersive powers are $\omega_A=0.04$ and $\omega_B=0.02$, where $\omega=(\mu_v-\mu_r)/(\mu_y-1)$. If the mean deviation is zero and the net violet–red angular separation is $0.04^\circ$, what are their apex angles $A_A$ and $A_B$?

verdicts.working: Zero mean deviation gives 0.5A_A=0.6A_B, so A_B=5A_A/6. The net color separation is |0.04(0.5A_A)-0.02(0.6A_B)|=0.01A_A=0.04°, hence A_A=4° and A_B=10/3°.

working:
$0.5A_A=0.6A_B\Rightarrow A_B=\frac56A_A$. Net angular separation $=\left[0.04(0.5)A_A-0.02(0.6)A_B\right]=0.01A_A=0.04^\circ$. Thus $A_A=4^\circ$ and $A_B=\frac{10}{3}^\circ$.

Independent check: Zero mean deviation gives 0.5A_A=0.6A_B, so A_B=5A_A/6. The net color separation is |0.04(0.5A_A)-0.02(0.6A_B)|=0.01A_A=0.04°, hence A_A=4° and A_B=10/3°.
